Process

How I build.

01
Define the problem before writing code

Every project starts with a specific, measurable gap. Not "I want to build an app" — but why this problem, why now, and why are existing solutions failing the people who have it. The build only starts when the problem is precise.

02
Design for the constraint, not the ideal

Most of my users are on low-end Android devices with inconsistent connectivity. Architecture decisions are made for those users first, not for the demo environment. Leaflet over Google Maps. Firebase over custom backend. Speed and reliability over feature count.

03
Ship the MVP. Get real feedback.

QUEVA launched with one core feature: PDF Q&A. 24 users tested it on launch day. Their feedback — not assumptions — became the entire v2 roadmap. Waiting for perfection is how products die before they ship.

04
Understand what you ship

I approach tools experimentally, testing, breaking, and comparing solutions before committing. AI accelerates the process. I take full ownership of the technical decisions behind what I build.

Cionti — Community of Talents in One Network — is a hyperlocal skill discovery platform built for Nigeria's informal economy. Think LinkedIn meets local search, designed specifically for the skilled workers in Effurun, Warri, and Delta State who have no digital presence despite genuine capability.

Type: Web App + Android (in active development)
Duration: Ideation 2023, active prototyping 2025, ongoing
Role: Solo Developer and Product Designer
Stack: HTML, CSS, Vanilla JS, Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage), Leaflet Maps, Paystack, Kotlin (Android)

View Live Prototype ↗ GitHub ↗

Nigeria's informal economy is one of the largest in Africa, yet the skilled workers who power it operate almost entirely without digital infrastructure. Mechanics, artisans, and creative professionals in cities like Effurun and Warri are discoverable only through personal referrals and physical proximity.

Why existing platforms fail
PlatformWhy it doesn't work
LinkedInFormal employment focus. No hyperlocal discovery. No informal sector support.
Fiverr / UpworkGlobal competition, dollar pricing, requires established rating history to gain any visibility.
Google MapsRequires a registered business entity. Excludes informal workers by default.
WhatsApp GroupsNo structure, no trust system, discovery limited to existing contacts only.

The consequence is a compounded market failure: skilled workers remain undermonetized despite genuine capability, and people seeking local help make decisions based on incomplete word-of-mouth. The gap is not a lack of ambition on either side. It is a lack of infrastructure built specifically for proximity-based, trust-weighted, informal-sector discovery in the Nigerian context. Cionti was built to close that gap.

Backend: Firebase

Firebase was selected as a deliberate constraint-driven decision. As a solo developer managing academics and product development simultaneously, a custom backend would have introduced unnecessary risk to the prototype timeline. Firebase provided real-time Firestore sync, auth, and storage with production-grade reliability and zero server management overhead. This is not a permanent decision — migration to Node.js or Go is planned once the product has validated market traction.

Maps: Leaflet over Google Maps SDK

Leaflet is fully open source with no API billing — eliminating financial exposure before the product generates revenue. It is also significantly lighter than the Google Maps SDK, producing faster load times on the lower-end devices that represent the target market.

The Trust Score Formula

The most deliberate architectural decision in the product. Ratings alone are the weakest signal because they are easiest to manipulate. A referral from a verified user carries social accountability — the person putting their own platform credibility behind it.

Trust Score = 0.5 × referrals + 0.3 × rating + 0.2 × verification

Together, these three weighted signals produce a trust profile structurally harder to inflate than any rating-only system.

Android: Kotlin with MVVM

MVVM architecture enforces separation between the data layer and UI layer from the start — a scalability decision that reduces the cost of future feature additions as the codebase grows toward a public launch.

Process

The prototype underwent five to eight full rebuilds. Each rebuild produced a cleaner separation of core features from non-essential ones. One significant setback — a system crash that lost substantial saved files and code — directly produced two permanent process changes: strict version control through Git and systematic cloud backup of all project assets.

Current status: Web prototype live and functional. Android build in parallel development. Both paused during the current academic semester — development resumes immediately post-exams.

✓
Web prototype live at obinna18.github.io/cionti-app
Core feature set fully implemented: skill profiles, map-based discovery, Firestore real-time sync, Paystack payment integration, Trust Score calculation.
✓

QUEVA is an AI-powered study companion built specifically for Nigerian university students. Upload any academic PDF, ask questions about its content, generate quiz questions for active recall practice, and export study outputs — all in one tool built for the realities of Nigerian campus life.

Type: AI-Powered Web App
Duration: 2025, active development ongoing
Role: Solo Developer and Product Designer
Stack: Vanilla JS, HTML, CSS, Firebase (Auth, Firestore), Groq API (LLaMA 3.3-70B), Vercel Proxy, PDF.js, jsPDF, EmailJS

Try QUEVA ↗ GitHub ↗

The Nigerian university academic calendar is structurally inconsistent. Lectures frequently start late into the semester, leaving students with a compressed study window before examinations. A student facing 200 to 300-page PDFs per course, across multiple courses simultaneously, with insufficient time to process them through conventional reading.

This is not a discipline problem. It is a density problem. The volume of material, compressed into an inadequate timeframe, makes traditional study methods ineffective for a student also managing extracurricular responsibilities, community commitments, and financial pressures simultaneously.

Why existing tools fail Nigerian students
ToolLimitation
ChatGPTPaid tier required for consistent use. Not optimized for document-specific Q&A.
NotebookLMNot widely accessible or optimized for Nigerian student workflows.
PDF SummarizersPassive output only. No interactive Q&A or quiz generation.
WhatsApp GroupsUnstructured, dependent on peers having correct information.

The need was not a general AI assistant. The need was a tool that could sit inside a specific PDF and answer specific questions about that material, on demand, in real time, for free.

AI Model Selection: Why Groq

The API selection process went through multiple iterations. Gemini was the first integration — abandoned because API keys expired mid-session with no reliable workaround, making it unusable in a study context where consistency is critical. A second API produced acceptable responses but failed to handle PDF content at required processing speed: three attempts to load a document would fail before one succeeded.

Groq with LLaMA 3.3-70B was selected for two factors: a generous free tier suitable for a student-facing product, and significantly faster inference speed than any alternative tested. For a study tool where a student is waiting on an answer, response latency directly affects usability. Groq's speed advantage was not marginal — it was the difference between a tool that felt alive and one that felt like a chore.

Security: Vercel Proxy

Calling the Groq API directly from the frontend would expose the API key in the browser — accessible to any user who inspects network requests. A Vercel serverless function was deployed as a proxy layer. All AI requests route through it, the key never touches the client, and Vercel's free tier covered deployment entirely. Security requirement and zero-cost infrastructure decision simultaneously.

PDF Processing: PDF.js

PDF.js parses uploaded documents and extracts text for AI context injection. One limitation discovered post-launch: PDF.js processes text layers only. PDFs containing scanned images or image-based content are not processable — this became a primary post-launch improvement target.

Origin of the idea

The concept originated directly from personal experience during examination season — facing multiple courses, each with hundreds of pages of PDF material and a compressed study timeline. The need for an interactive, document-aware study tool became concrete and immediate rather than theoretical.

✓
Live at obinna18.github.io/QUEVA
PDF upload, document-specific Q&A, quiz generation, result export via jsPDF, Firebase Auth session persistence — all fully functional.
24

✓

01
Image-based PDF support
Most frequently reported limitation on launch day. Adding OCR via Tesseract.js or a cloud OCR API would allow QUEVA to process scanned documents — a significant portion of Nigerian university study material.
02
RAG implementation
Currently the full PDF text is injected into the AI context. Retrieval-Augmented Generation would allow QUEVA to retrieve only the most relevant sections per query, improving accuracy on large documents.
03
Gemini reintegration
Gemini remains a target once a robust API key rotation and session management strategy is in place. Its capabilities are well-suited to document-specific Q&A at scale.
04
Onboarding flow
First-time users needed more guidance on how to interact effectively. A structured onboarding sequence would reduce the initial friction some launch-day users experienced.
05
Monetization tier
Free plan for basic PDF Q&A. Paid plan for unlimited uploads, deeper document analysis, and priority inference. Not yet implemented.

A full business management suite built for Hems & Gents, a fashion brand operating across Lagos. The system handles customer-facing product browsing, in-platform payment via Paystack, automated receipt generation, and a real-time admin dashboard — all accessible from the owner's phone as the primary device.

Type: Web App — Freelance Client Project
Duration: January 2026, completed
Role: Solo Developer
Stack: HTML, CSS, Vanilla JS, Firebase (Auth, Firestore), Paystack, EmailJS, GitHub Pages

View Live ↗

Hems & Gents was operating without digital infrastructure. Orders were tracked manually, receipts issued by hand, and payment collection happened informally with no reliable record system. As the brand grew, the manual approach created compounding gaps: lost orders, payment disputes, no visibility into outstanding balances, and no way for customers to browse and place orders outside of direct contact.

The business needed a system that could handle customer-facing ordering, in-platform payment, automated receipt generation, and an admin dashboard that gave the owner full real-time visibility — without requiring technical knowledge to operate daily.

Firebase Firestore

Every transaction writes to Firestore immediately, giving the owner a live dashboard that reflects the current state of the business without manual updates. No refresh required — the state is always current.

Paystack Integration

Paystack was selected because it is the dominant Nigerian payment gateway with strong support for local bank transfers, USSD, and card payments — the actual payment methods the brand's customers use.

WhatsApp Number Normalization

WhatsApp order notifications were implemented with phone number normalization to handle the Nigerian number format inconsistency (+234 vs 0 prefix) that caused notification failures during early testing.

Mobile Chrome Fixes

Several mobile-specific bugs required targeted fixes: delete button failures on Android Chrome caused by event propagation in dynamically built HTML, and a custom modal system replacing native browser confirm() dialogs that behave unpredictably on mobile Chrome.

Scope Evolution

The client brief was a working storefront with payment. The scope expanded through the build as real operational needs became clear — the receipt system, admin dashboard, and outstanding balance tracker were all added in response to actual client workflow rather than the original spec.

A 40-module interactive digital education platform covering income streams for young Nigerians. Sold via Selar with an access code gate. Self-contained single HTML file — no backend, no monthly cost, full margin retained.

Type: Digital Product — Web SPA
Duration: 2025, active
Role: Solo Developer and Content Creator
Stack: HTML, CSS, Vanilla JS, GitHub Pages, Selar

View Platform ↗ Buy on Selar ↗

Most income education content targeted at young Nigerians is either locked behind expensive courses on foreign platforms, distributed as low-quality PDFs with no structure, or scattered across social media with no coherent learning path.

A student or young professional who wants to understand digital income streams, freelancing, and financial independence has no affordable, structured, locally relevant resource they can work through systematically. The gap is not a lack of information — it is a lack of organized, actionable, affordable education built for the Nigerian young adult context.

Single-file SPA architecture

The platform is a single HTML file served via GitHub Pages. No server, no database, no API — everything runs statically. This eliminates hosting complexity, removes all operational cost, and means the product is infinitely scalable with no infrastructure overhead.

Access code system

The access code is embedded directly in the file. Selar handles payment processing and receipt delivery, and the buyer receives a code that unlocks the platform on their device. The entire distribution pipeline runs at zero operational cost.

Why not Teachable or Kajabi

Platform fees on tools like Teachable or Kajabi take 5–10% of every transaction. Selar charges a flat processing fee with no revenue share. Owning the delivery infrastructure means the full margin stays with the product. Building it rather than renting a platform was a deliberate margin decision.

Product structure

40 modules across 7 tiers: freelancing, digital products, content monetization, affiliate models, service businesses, investing basics, and AI-assisted income generation. Each module has a downloadable PDF component for offline access in variable connectivity environments.

A private, secure payment tracking dashboard built for Giddel Consult, a consulting firm managing a recurring book of clients with outstanding fees. Firebase-backed with real-time sync — the owner always sees the current state of receivables without a page refresh.

Type: Web App — Freelance Client Project
Duration: 2026, completed
Role: Solo Developer
Stack: HTML, CSS, Vanilla JS, Firebase (Auth, Firestore), GitHub Pages

Giddel Consult managed its outstanding client fees across spreadsheets, notes, and memory. As the client list grew, the manual system produced errors, missed follow-ups, and no single reliable source of truth for the firm's receivables.

The need was a private, secure dashboard that showed the firm's complete payment position at a glance, allowed new records to be added quickly, and updated in real time so the owner was never working from stale data.

Firebase Auth — Private by Default

The dashboard is locked behind Firebase Auth. No unauthenticated access, no public-facing data. The firm's payment records are private by architecture, not just by obscurity.

Real-time Firestore Sync

Any update reflects immediately across all authenticated sessions without a page refresh. The owner and any authorized team member always see the same live data.

Design philosophy: operational speed

Adding a client, recording a payment, and updating an outstanding balance should each take under 30 seconds. No complexity was added that was not explicitly required by the client's workflow. Simple is correct when the user's job is tracking money, not navigating software.

DLCF FUPRE · Academic Unit Designer
DLCF Design Work
Campaign Design Infographic Canva Social Media

Volunteer designer for the Academic Unit of Deeper Life Campus Fellowship (TETFUND) — FUPRE. Created student-facing social media content across motivation, academic accountability, and community engagement themes.

The Brief

Content that speaks to a FUPRE student's actual academic experience — not generic Christian motivational graphics, but material that acknowledges the real pressure of campus life and addresses it directly.

The Design Problem

Most campus Christian content defaults to gold-and-white stock imagery with Bible verses in decorative fonts. That aesthetic is familiar to the point of invisibility — students scroll past it without processing it. The challenge was standing out in a student's feed without losing the fellowship's identity.

Why Dark Backgrounds

Dark-background content creates immediate contrast against the predominantly white UI of Instagram and WhatsApp, drawing the eye before the message is even read. The decision was to go typography-led and message-forward — visual weight sits on the words, not the decoration. A student should read the core message in under three seconds while scrolling.

Typography Rationale

Typography selection prioritized legibility at small sizes over stylistic personality. Strong weight contrast between headline and supporting copy — one thing dominates, everything else supports it. The goal: a student reading on a cracked-screen Android at low brightness could still read the content without effort.

Color Philosophy

Color was used as a signal, not decoration. A consistent accent color across the series makes every card immediately recognizable as belonging to the same source — a student who sees one card in a friend's status instantly recognizes the next one in the feed.

Stay Grounded Campaign

Mid-semester drift is a real and universal experience for FUPRE students — the point where early-semester discipline breaks down. The design acknowledged that reality directly rather than offering generic encouragement. The message does not pretend the pressure does not exist. It meets the student inside it.

Before Class Checklist

Designed as a utility post rather than a motivational one. Students could screenshot and actually use it. The layout mimicked the visual logic of a real checklist — items spaced for readability, hierarchy clear — so it functioned as a genuine tool, not content designed to be consumed and forgotten.

Academic FAQ Series

Converted recurring unit questions into shareable designed cards. Consistent format so every card in the series was immediately recognizable as belonging to the same source. Repeatability was the design goal: a student who shares one card is effectively distributing the unit's brand without knowing it.

DSN FUPRE · Chapter Lead
DSN FUPRE Design Work
Recruitment Campaign Canva Social Media

Data Science Nigeria — FUPRE Chapter. As Chapter Lead, designed recruitment and engagement content for the chapter's WhatsApp onboarding campaign and social media presence. The primary design challenge: communicate a technical community to a general student audience without making it feel intimidating or exclusive.

Join DSN FUPRE ↗
The Core Tension

Go too technical and you only reach people already in the field — defeating the recruitment purpose. Go too casual and you undermine the chapter's seriousness as a professional development community. The solution: a tech-forward aesthetic built on clean geometry, structured layouts, and a limited color palette — visual signals that communicate organization and precision without requiring the viewer to understand the subject matter to feel the credibility.

Color Rationale

The palette drew from standard tech-industry visual language: dark backgrounds, accent colors in blue or teal, white type. These are not arbitrary choices — they are the colors associated with terminals, dashboards, and developer tools. A student who sees them instinctively reads "technical" and "professional" before processing a single word. The color palette does the positioning before the copy does.

Typography and Hierarchy

Hierarchy was strict. Chapter name, then value proposition, then call to action — in that order, at decreasing visual weight. No element competed with the primary message. This matters especially for WhatsApp distribution where graphics are viewed at thumbnail size before being tapped open. The headline has to communicate on its own before the image is even opened.

Holiday Campaign — a Retention Strategy

Maintaining visibility during academic breaks was deliberate, not filler. Students who see the community consistently present during downtime remain engaged when the semester resumes. A chapter that goes silent in December reactivates to a colder audience in January. The holiday content kept the community warm.

Recruitment Graphics

Specific value propositions rather than generic join-us messaging. Each graphic communicated one concrete thing: what skill you gain, what community you enter, what the chapter connects you to. Specificity was the differentiator from other campus organizations who post vague "come be part of something great" content that communicates nothing.

Freelance · Independent Clients
Freelance Design Work
Brand Identity Product Ad Adobe Illustrator Canva

Independent freelance design commissions and redesign practice. Two projects: a product launch ad for AeroPure Mini, and a brand flyer redesign exercise for Emily Glam Studio.

The Brief

A launch ad for AeroPure Mini — a compact smart air purifier targeting urban Nigerian households concerned about indoor air quality. Communicate the product's core value without relying on technical specifications most consumers would not engage with.

Why Lead with Outcome, Not Mechanism

Product ads in the Nigerian market often try to communicate everything at once — price, features, specs, and a call to action in one graphic. The result is visual noise where nothing is memorable. The decision was to lead with one message: the outcome, not the mechanism. What does this product do for your life? Not how does it work.

Color Rationale

Clean whites and light neutrals were chosen to visually reinforce the product's value proposition — purity, cleanliness, freshness. The color palette communicates the message before the copy is read. Warm accents prevented the layout from feeling clinical. Target placement was Instagram and WhatsApp status — fast-scroll environments where you have under two seconds. The palette does the first second of work.

Typography

Minimal. Large headline stating the outcome, small supporting text for the product name and key detail. Nothing competes with the central message. Modern-sans — clean, neutral, not trying to be clever. The font gets out of the way of the message.

Context

This was a redesign exercise rather than an original commission. An existing flyer was taken and rebuilt from scratch as a design practice project — exploring how different decisions about color, type, and layout could serve the same brief more effectively.

The Design Problem

A beauty studio launch flyer that reads as luxury without feeling cold — a common and genuinely difficult design problem. Luxury can easily slide into intimidating. Warmth can easily slide into cheap. The redesign was an exercise in holding both at once.

Color Rationale

Warm gold palette. Gold communicates premium and aspiration in the beauty market — a color with existing cultural associations that does meaning-making before the viewer consciously processes it. The warmth in the tone prevented it from reading as cold luxury.

Typography Choice

Oversized serif as the primary visual element. Serifs carry inherent associations with craft, tradition, and quality — a deliberate choice for a brand positioning itself as premium rather than budget. The frosted card overlay for service listing created visual layering without adding complexity.

What the Redesign Explored

How much weight typography alone can carry when the photographic treatment supports it. The light-leak photography treatment added warmth and texture that a clean studio photo would not have provided. In beauty marketing, how something makes you feel at first glance is more important than what it tells you.
